A "Bachelor of Arts in Combination" Public Safety degree is typically an interdisciplinary program designed for individuals who already possess a two-year college diploma in a public safety field. This degree completion program builds upon existing credentials to confer a four-year degree. The curriculum integrates public safety-specific courses with subjects such as leadership, political science, and health sciences, equipping students with advanced analytical, critical thinking, and leadership skills necessary for career advancement.

The program aims to provide students with competencies in critical thinking, analytical reasoning, communication, and data analysis to facilitate the acquisition of actionable intelligence.

Make a meaningful impact in the community and cultivate the critical thinking skills essential for any career related to public safety. Learn from dedicated professors with real-world experience and join the ranks of graduates who have successfully pursued careers in mental health, government, and communications after graduating from this university.
11ea:
Program Description

Criminology students will explore the intricate dynamics of crime, criminals, victims, and the legal system. Unlike an episode of CSI, while forensic science is a component of their studies, the curriculum also incorporates sociology, psychology, and law to analyze the definition of crime, the motivations behind criminal behavior, and societal responses.

Criminologists concentrate on:

  • Theories that elucidate the causes of crime.
  • The social consequences and reactions to crime and deviance.
  • Victimization.
  • The criminal justice system and law enforcement responses, as well as crime prevention strategies.

Students are encouraged to adopt an interdisciplinary approach that integrates sociology, psychology, and law. They will engage with real-world challenges and strive to find effective solutions to the social issues associated with crime and victimization.
11dc:
Bachelor of Science (BSc) in Computer Science equips students with robust skills in algorithm analysis and design across procedural, object-oriented, and low-level programming languages, while also offering an optional introduction to functional, parallel, and logical paradigms.

The faculty recognizes that hands-on experience is crucial for a comprehensive understanding of computing fundamentals; therefore, students will engage extensively in laboratory work. In their senior years, they will have the opportunity to select courses in various application areas, including internet computing, mobile application development, applied cryptography, and quantum computing. Furthermore, students will acquire essential experience in collaborative work, project management, and time management.

The Computer Science program provides students with exposure not only to software but also to the hardware that underpins computer and embedded systems. This dual focus fosters a fundamental understanding of digital systems and microprocessors, as well as an appreciation for the interplay between hardware and software.
11eq:
Program Description

Social work is a practice-based profession that uses human rights and social justice principles to empower those disadvantaged by class, race, gender, age, and ability.

Laurier's Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) offers a holistic, interdisciplinary academic experience that shapes your identity as a social worker.

This direct-entry program allows you to study social work from the first year. In senior years, you'll gain supervised pre-professional experience through two field placements in social and community agencies. Graduating will equip you with effective communication and ethical practice skills.

Master of Science in Management Analytics (MMA) and Master of Finance (MFin) double degree is combined with experiential learning to help students gain comprehensive knowledge both in finance and data analytics as well as hands-on experience for solving real-world finance problems using sophisticated analytical tools and quantitative models.

The next evolution of finance is underway with machine learning and advanced data analytics. Join this dynamic industry by earning a double degree in Master of Science in Management Analytics (MMA) and Master of Finance (MFin). The integrated curriculum offers experiential learning, providing comprehensive knowledge in finance and data analytics while solving real-world finance problems with analytical tools and quantitative models.

Students will gain expertise in both theoretical and practical finance aspects, including financial engineering and data-driven decision-making through management analytics.
6ckh:
Applied Computing (MAC) is a postgraduate degree focused on applying computer science to solve real-world problems. The curriculum emphasizes industry-relevant skills like software design, data analysis, and coding through coursework and projects, preparing graduates for immediate tech employment. "MAC" stands for Master of Applied Computing.

This advanced degree evolves with technology, focusing on mobile, enterprise, data mining, and machine learning, helping students excel in the job market with advanced technical skills for creating tech solutions.

The programs blend core computing skills with specialization tracks and integrate elements from other disciplines, providing job-ready skills and emphasizing problem-solving.

The curriculum exposes students to the latest technologies in high-demand fields.
6rnp:
The Master of Applied Computing (MAC) offers an advanced computing degree that adapts with the ever-changing technological landscape through a theoretical, practical and in-demand program focused on mobile, enterprise, data mining and machine learning.

The MAC program will help students stand out in the job market and proves to employers that you have advanced technical knowledge and skills required to create technological solutions.

In the full-time coursework option, students will complete nine courses. It is anticipated that it will take four terms (16 months) to complete this degree. Required courses include:

  • CP600: Practical Algorithm Design (in person)
  • CP683: Graduate Project
  • Seven elective courses at the 600 level from those offered by the program.
6y55:
The Master of Applied Politics (MAP) program attracts recent graduates seeking a competitive advantage in their careers, as well as mature students aiming for professional advancement. Participants acquire essential skills in policy analysis, electoral and media analysis, survey design, and problem-solving, while gaining practical experience through placements with community organizations, local politicians, and government agencies.

Students develop critical competencies—such as policy analysis, electoral and media analysis, survey instrument design, and problem-solving in both domestic and international contexts—and gain hands-on experience through placements with community organizations, local politicians, and government agencies.

Research Expertise

Our faculty provides research expertise in the following areas:

  • International relations and cross-border governance.
  • Public policy (social, aboriginal, environmental, multicultural, migration).
  • International political economy and trade.
  • Public opinion, elections, and political parties.
  • Canadian politics (multi-level governance, Quebec).
  • Area studies (North America, Africa, Europe, Asia, Latin America).
  • International human rights.
6w0x:
A Social Justice and Community Engagement (MA) is a master's degree program that prepares students to address social inequalities through a combination of theoretical knowledge, practical skills, and real-world community-based experience.

This program fosters the student's ability to investigate and understand the root causes of the most pertinent social justice and environmental issues of our times. Through a combination of critical theory, methods, and an individualized community placement, this Master of Arts (MA) program in Social Justice and Community Engagement (SJCE) engages students in the active promotion of social and environmental justice principles within our communities and around the world.

Through coursework, an individualized community placement and either practice-focused courses or a major research paper (MRP), students will develop knowledge that contributes to their own understanding of how to make change in the world, as well as the skills that facilitate the development of communities to undertake social justice and environmental work.
6y56:
Master of Arts in Business Economics (MABE) program prepares students for a career as professional economists in both the private and public sectors. Its strength lies in the integration of business economics with comprehensive training in economic theory, quantitative methods, and applied research.

Students can develop the skills that employers seek through the co-op option. This option provides valuable professional experience and expands students' networks within a timeframe of four to eight months, in addition to the 12 months of coursework. Furthermore, this opportunity allows students to apply the knowledge and skills acquired in the classroom, gain new insights, and enhance their employment prospects.
6w0k:
Master of Arts (MA) in Criminology is an intensive program designed to cultivate foundational knowledge in research practices, theories of crime and deviance, and professional development opportunities. This program promotes professional growth and leadership by encouraging students to engage in critical thinking processes while offering avenues for investigative research into contemporary issues related to criminology and society.

The 12-month coursework stream will be completed over three consecutive terms. The program provides students with advanced coursework that equips them with the essential skills to locate, evaluate, and synthesize existing evidence-based research. Additionally, students will develop leadership, analytical, and research skills. The competencies acquired from this program will prepare students for applied work in the field and equip them with the necessary skills to become professional social researchers in both private and public sectors.

The dynamic and engaging Master of Arts (MA) in Criminology program offers applicants critical analysis, theoretical and methodological training opportunities, as well as substantive knowledge on topics pertinent to criminology and criminal justice. These topics may include, but are not limited to, culture, crime and policy, comparative and international criminology and criminal justice, policing, and media criminology.
732u:
User Experience (UX) Design involves creating user-friendly experiences across digital and other products or services. These solutions apply to web, 3D, and various services.mobile apps, physical spaces, immersive design, and complex digital systems. UX professionals are highly sought after, ranking among the top 10 jobs globally due to their value across industries like retail, medicine, technology, finance, education, and government.

The Master of Science (MSc) in UX User Experience Design at Wilfrid Laurier University prepares students for UX careers through practical learning, helping them build a CV and job-ready portfolio. Wilfrid Laurier University offers a broad approach to UX design, covering digital solutions, services, and immersive spaces. Students learn UX theory and tools, gaining hands-on training in psychology, research methods, design thinking, business strategy, prototyping, usability testing, and interface design.

Program Highlights

  • Build your portfolio from the first semester, working on real projects with industry, government, and community clients. Collaborate with UX professionals to learn the entire UX process, preparing for high-demand roles in business, tech, government, and health.
  • Get experience designing digital interfaces, physical products and services, and immersive environments in one of Canada’s only graduate programs in the field.
  • A competitive-entry eight-month co-op opportunity is available. Students interested in the co-op stream must select that option at the time of application. Students who apply and are admitted to the coursework stream will work on a client project in their final semester.

Since 1976, the Lazaridis Master of Business Administration (MBA) program has offered a world-class business education, being the first Canadian university to provide a one-year, full-time MBA with an intensive core curriculum.

The Lazaridis MBA is flexible, catering to recent graduates seeking co-op experience or working professionals advancing their careers, allowing students to choose their preferred delivery format. All students share a strong foundation, including a common core curriculum, hands-on experiential learning, and small classes with award-winning faculty.

With dedicated career services and professional development support, every pathway equips student to apply the learning in real time, graduating as a confident, career-ready leader.
6w0t:
Since 1976, the Lazaridis Master of Business Administration (MBA) program has provided an innovative, world-class business education. It was the first Canadian university to offer a one-year, full-time MBA for those seeking the degree quickly, featuring an intensive core curriculum that exposes students to key disciplines concurrently.

The Full-Time MBA + co-op program is aimed at high-caliber, recent graduates with under two years of work experience. For those seeking valuable real-life experience or transitioning to a new industry, this program offers eight months of work experience, enhancing resumes and providing insights for career decisions.

Wilfrid Laurier University hosts Ontario's first business co-op program and now has Canada's largest business degree co-op program. We are accredited by Co-operative Education and Work-Integrated Learning Canada (CEWIL Canada) for meeting high standards. The Lazaridis Full-Time MBA + Co-op program is the first MBA co-op program in Canada to receive this prestigious accreditation.
